doc.title: Dick Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: How the Catatonic Five got its name
summary: Derry Hall proposed the Great Five; Sherman suggested Catatonic Five from abnormal psychology, and they banter about band names.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: Is there a story behind the name Catatonic Five?
Yes. Derry Hall and I were kicking around what name to give this band. He said, “Let’s name it the Great Five.”

The Great Five, how can you argue with that? And I had just been studying a little abnormal psychology and I said, “How about the Catatonic Five?” He says, “What is catatonia?” And I said, “It is this state of psychosis which is marked by wax-like immobility interrupted by sudden fits of frenzy.” He said, “That’s it, we’ll name it the Catatonic Five.” © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-
That’s terrific. That’s good. Well you know there’s been plenty of odd band names over the years.
Really. They seem odder but you know, at the time you had the Mound City Blues Blowers and those kinds of things. But I like the name, it has a certain ring to it.
Catatonic. Yeah, it’s got tonic in it and it’s got cat.
Yeah. And you can always change the number in case you have another member.
The Catatonic Six has a good ring to it also.
